messages:
incident-bot: Pager: SEV2 - repeated CrashLoopBackOff for model-serving pods in cluster eu-central-gpu. Symptom: runtime process segfaulting during model warmup on many pods. Affected deployment: model-serving-v3 (approx 20 pods). Escalating to oncall-lee.

oncall-lee: Ack. Jumping in. Any indicator of memory pressure or driver errors?

sre-anne: grabbing pod logs from model-serving-v3-5f9c:
```
2026-03-15T08:05:11Z INFO loading model gpt-slim-trt
2026-03-15T08:05:12Z ERROR runtime: signal 11 at 0x7fffab12d400
2026-03-15T08:05:12Z ERROR backtrace: libtrt_fused.so(+0x3f2b0)
2026-03-15T08:05:12Z ERROR container exiting with status 139
```

eng-runtime-oliver: That backtrace points to the fused TRT kernels. Do we have a recent driver or kernel change in eu-central? @infra-raj

infra-raj: We applied a security kernel update overnight to nodes gpu-a..gpu-d; driver version on gpu-c didn't rotate correctly and remains older. Listing nodes shows gpu-c with slightly different CUDA driver (520.x vs 525.x).

eng-ml-zoe: The affected customers are using long-context sessions with large KV caches and batch spikes around 08:00. Could be hitting a combined OOM+kernel bug.

support-lina: Customer X reported intermittent 5xxs starting ~08:03, they're on Dedicated in eu-central. I'm notifying them that we're investigating.

oncall-lee: Immediate plan: 1) disable TRT fused kernels on new pods (REDWOOD_TRT_FUSED=0), 2) reduce MAX_BATCH_TOKENS to 800, 3) cordon gpu-c and move pods, 4) shift traffic to fallback quantized pool. Applying 1-3 now.

sre-anne: Running commands:
```
kubectl -n prod set env deployment/model-serving-v3 REDWOOD_TRT_FUSED=0 --all
kubectl -n prod set env deployment/model-serving-v3 REDWOOD_MAX_BATCH_TOKENS=800 --all
kubectl cordon gpu-c && kubectl drain gpu-c --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data
kubectl -n prod rollout restart deployment/model-serving-v3
```

eng-runtime-oliver: Also recommend REDWOOD_KV_CACHE_MAX=256MB to limit per-worker KV.

infra-raj: cordon/drain in progress. Some pods restarted but a subset goes straight to CrashLoopBackOff with immediate segfault. Collecting dmesg from gpu-b and gpu-c.

sre-anne: dmesg excerpt from gpu-c:
```
[Thu Mar 15 08:05:12] Out of memory: Killed process 45678 (runtime)
[Thu Mar 15 08:05:12] oom_reaper: reaped process 45678
[Thu Mar 15 08:05:12] kernel: segfault at 0 ip 00007fffae123f40 sp 00007fffb12ab280 error 4 in libtrt_fused.so
```

eng-runtime-oliver: That matches an OOM-triggered segfault in the fused kernel path. Likely race where allocator returns null and kernel dereferences. Workaround is fine for now; need a kernel-side guard. I'll open runtime ticket.

oncall-lee: I'm starting a small canary pod with the non-fused env to validate model init.

sre-anne: Canary logs show successful init with REDWOOD_TRT_FUSED=0. No segfaults, model warmup completes.

infra-raj: Node gpu-c rebooted and rejoined with driver 525.105 after manual remediation. Monitoring for page-faults.

support-lina: Updating customers: we've routed traffic away from affected nodes and are rolling a non-fused variant. Offering status update to affected accounts.

oncall-lee: Observability note: token throughput dropped and tail latency increased for eu-central between 08:03-08:12 while pods restarted. Number of 5xxs peaked ~08:06. Marking customer impact for Dedicated tenants in that region.

eng-ml-zoe: Additional mitigation: enable aggressive KV eviction on affected pods with REDWOOD_KV_CACHE_MAX=150MB and set REDWOOD_CACHE_EVICT_POLICY=LRU for now.

sre-anne: Deploy update applied; CrashLoopBackOff count down from 20 to 4 as more pods come up with non-fused runtime.

oncall-lee: If stable in next 15m, we'll shift impacted customers back to normal pool gradually. Otherwise keep them on CPU-quant fallback.

eng-runtime-oliver: Long-term work: 1) add null-checks and OOM-safe paths in fused kernels, 2) unit/regression test for long-context + large-batch which previously tripped this, 3) add automated fallback rule: if segfault rate > 2/min then flip REDWOOD_TRT_FUSED=0 for that deployment.

oncall-jordan: Taking over oncall after Lee. If you don't close before handoff, I'll continue monitoring.

incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-3121 created and assigned. Severity updated to SEV3 after partial mitigation.

support-lina: Customers notified and incident timeline being updated. We'll coordinate SLA remediation if they exceed error thresholds.

oncall-jordan: Closing live triage thread. Will follow up with postmortem owners and schedule a bug review with eng-runtime + eng-ml. Thanks all :thumbsup:
